findings.title: Denial cache pins false denies and skips permission refresh
findings.body: Check writes a 30s denial (userPermDenialCacheKey) whenever the DB-backed check returns false, and the next Check returns that denial before consulting either the permission cache or the database. A negative result is often stale rather than authoritative: checkInheritedPermissions uses the separately cached folder tree, so a dashboard/folder under a newly created parent is denied even when the user has folders:uid:<parent> (or a permission row that was committed after the check). That false deny is then sticky for shortCacheTTL, including after the folder cache expires and after a later grant, which re-breaks the create-then-access case this PR is fixing. Denial entries are never deleted on a successful refresh.

findings.title: Cached check error skips the DB permission fallback
findings.body: If getCachedIdentityPermissions hits but checkPermission fails (typically buildFolderTree / folder store error while evaluating inheritance), Check returns the error immediately. It never reaches getIdentityPermissions, so a direct scope that exists only in the DB (the newly created dashboard/folder permission this change is meant to observe) is never loaded. A transient folder-store failure therefore fails the request even when the refreshed permission set would allow without walking the folder tree.

findings.title: Warm permission cache no longer serves distinct denies
findings.body: A permission-cache hit that does not contain the requested scope is treated as a miss and always calls getIdentityPermissions, which no longer reads the cache and always queries the DB (and then overwrites permCache). Previously one cached scope map answered every Check for that user and action. Now each distinct denied (namespace, user, action, name, folder) tuple hits the database until its denial entry is warm. Authorizing a page or search over many resources the user cannot access becomes a query stampede, and concurrent refreshes can also overwrite a newer permCache entry with an older snapshot.
